A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are sufficiently complete and readable for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on watermark forgery and removal, including baseline comparisons, transferability tests, robustness analyses, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised and additional image-quality measurements.

M1.justification: The Imprint-Forgery and Imprint-Removal objectives, masking extension, Reprompting procedure, and multiple-prompt/bin-resampling augmentations are unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image and prompt datasets, including MS-COCO-2017, Stable-Diffusion-Prompts, I2P, and Anime-with-caption-CC0. The forgery, removal, transferability, and image-perturbation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Averaging for forgery and Averaging, Regeneration, AdvEmb, and Surrogate for removal. Additional reference-image counts configure the existing Averaging baseline rather than introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds LPIPS to the main image-quality evaluation and LPIPS/MS-SSIM to Tables 4–5, and reports a PSNR processing correction. Appendix C also includes 50 references in its stated averaging sweep. Retained experiments keep their datasets, attack budgets, sample counts, and detection thresholds.

E4.justification: Corrected PSNR measurements revise the attack-success/image-quality analysis in Figure 16 and the quality results of the sampler/inversion-step ablation in Figure 19. The tested questions remain the same; the transferability, perturbation-robustness, and finetuning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report dispersion values in Tables 4–5 and use boxplots. The 30 randomly sampled reference sets are unchanged. Added quality metrics follow the existing reporting style; changed dispersion values do not establish a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: PSNR corrections substantially revise the image-quality results. For Gaussian Shading on SD2.1-Anime at 150 Imprint-Forgery steps, Table 1 changes PSNR from 29.78 to 20.11 while detection and attribution remain 1.00. v3 also adds LPIPS/MS-SSIM measurements and expands appendix result tabulations. The correction notice attributes the PSNR changes to processing errors, rather than changed attack performance.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, attack losses, watermark definitions, statistical assumptions, and attribution-threshold relationship in Equation (6) are unchanged. No new theoretical results or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: single-reference black-box attacks transfer across unrelated models, enable forgery and removal, and cannot be defeated simply by tightening detection thresholds.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes the assertion that attacks preserve image quality 'in all cases' to 'often.' It acknowledges low PSNR and proposes latent-space edge shifts as an explanation. Figure 17 adds a qualification about PSNR's imperfect correspondence with visible quality, and Appendix C removes the assertion that the proposed attack has no strong distortions.

D1.justification: v3 adds a PSNR processing-error notice directing readers to the existing repository for details. Appendix C explicitly lists the 50-reference averaging configuration, already illustrated in v2's Figure 17. Appendix D's implementation settings, hardware, runtimes, and resource links are otherwise retained; the correction procedure itself is not specified locally.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhang et al.'s 2018 perceptual-metric paper to support LPIPS. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous watermark attacks remain unchanged; subsequent reference-number changes do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the image-quality discussion, the processing-error footnote, Appendix C, and figure/table captions. The title, section organization, method exposition, and most other prose are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain LPIPS columns and 20-step rows previously available in the appendix. Tables 4–5 are reorganized and compressed for additional columns and rows. Existing example figures gain metric annotations, and Figures 16 and 19 receive revised PSNR axes and curves.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs an important weakness in the evidence for attack practicality: inflated PSNR measurements supported v2's categorical image-quality assertion. The explicit correction, substantially revised values in Tables 1–2, complementary LPIPS/MS-SSIM measurements, and narrower interpretation make the quality-versus-success evaluation considerably more credible. The exact processing fix remains deferred to the repository, limiting local reproducibility, but the correction and qualification provide a substantial net improvement.
